Hi Naomi,

Thanks for taking this on. Greenline is collecting SIG (SIG Lite) evidence for our vendor risk review and we need a concise package of artifacts and a short annotated trace showing how our SDLC controls are implemented end-to-end for Redwood Inference. Specifically we are asking for: 

- A short narrative describing the code review and PR gating process (who approves, required checks).
- CI/CD pipeline screenshots or a simple export showing pipeline stages and gating rules.
- Proof of secret handling and rotation (keystore ownership, rotation cadence, ephemeral creds).
- Change management evidence for production releases (change log, approval stamps).
- Any policy documents or playbooks referenced.

If possible, please bundle files and include an index with brief notes mapping items to the SIG question ids. Our deadline for the first bundle is 2028-05-03 COB.

Thanks — I can extend if you need more time, but please confirm receipt and an ETA.

Regards,

Naomi / Jordan — attaching the CI artifacts we can provide.

Summary (short):
- CI uses staged pipelines in GitLab (dev -> staging -> prod). Each merge to main triggers the full pipeline; merges require 2 approvers and passing unit + integration + security-scan jobs.
- Gating: OPA policy checks run as part of the pipeline (policy-check job) and block deploy jobs if violations are found. We maintain a small allowlist for infra changes that require additional approvals.
- Export: attached pipeline YAML for the prod pipeline (pipeline-prod.yaml) and 3 screenshots that show the gating jobs.

Attachments: [Attachment: pipeline-prod.yaml (text)], [Attachment: ci_pipeline_screenshots_2028-04-30.pdf]

Notes on secrets in CI: we inject ephemeral tokens from our internal Vault (HashiCorp) at job runtime. Jobs never write secrets to logs; the Vault token is short-lived and limited to the job scope. Rotation is automated (see Monica's log).

Happy to provide more granular logs if Greenline needs timestamps for a sampling.

— Karthik
Senior SRE

Marta — attaching the requested development-controls package for Greenline's SIG review. Bundle includes an index that maps each file to the SIG question set. Quick notes below and items attached: 

Index (high level):
1) Narrative: dev_controls_narrative.txt — brief description of PR gating, reviewer roles, canary deployments, and rollback policy.
2) CI: pipeline-prod.yaml + ci_pipeline_screenshots_2028-04-30.pdf — shows gating jobs and OPA check.
3) Secrets: keystore_rotation_log_2028-04.csv + rotation_ticket_RG-4356.pdf — rotation cadence and recent change record.
4) Change management: deploy_changelog_q1-q2_2028.pdf — annotated production release entries with approver initials.
5) Policy: sd_dev_playbook_v2.1.pdf — development playbook and release checklist.

Attachments: [Attachment: greenline_dev_controls_bundle_2028-04-30.zip] (contains the files listed above)

A few clarifications in case they help with mapping to SIG IDs:
- Code review: all merges to main require two reviewers; at least one reviewer must be an engineer other than the author and at least one automated security check must pass (SAST + dependency-scan).
- CI gating: policy-check (OPA) is enforced as a pre-deploy job and will fail the pipeline if a rule is violated; deploy jobs are gated by an explicit manual approval step for production.
- Secrets: production secrets are stored in an HSM-backed KMS; application services request scoped tokens from Vault with a 1-hour TTL by default.
- Change approvals: the deploy_changelog has traceable approvals; emergency changes are routed via an on-call escalation that produces an approval ticket (see RG-4356).

If you want additional evidence (e.g., timestamped sampling of pipeline runs or raw job logs), let me know which SIG IDs you want sampled and we can pull a time-limited bundle.

Best,
Naomi Feldman
Director, Security & Compliance (Eng)
Redwood Inference
